newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close down 1.41 pct, tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close down 1.41 pct, tight liquidity.

text.p: Ongoing tight liquidity in the money market and investor worries that the baht might ease further against the dollar sparked selling and drove the index down 1.41 percent at the close on Monday, brokers said.

"Liquidity was still tight in the money market today after the Chinese New Year and commercial banks reserve requirements last week. Also, investors were a bit concerned that the baht would fall against the dollar in medium-term," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
The SET index closed 10.53 points lower to 737.23 on 2.4 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index retreated 1.05 points to 53.68.
Decliners trounced gainers 217 to 81 while 86 issues were unchanged.
"I think that most investors were sidelined today because they wanted to have a clearer picture about the foreign exchange market before entering the market again," Thanawat said.
The Bank of Thailand set the midrate on Monday at 25.90 baht a dollar versus 25.92 on Friday.
The overnight interbank rate slipped to about 20 percent late on Monday compared to 24-25 percent early in the day.
Brokers said sales of stocks mainly in the banking and finance sectors forced the composite SET index down.

Bangkok Bank topped the active list, falling one baht to 173. PTT Exploration and Production gained four to 324 while large capitalised Finance One slipped 0.50 to 30.50 and Siam Cement, Thailand's largest cement manufacturer, dropped 24 to 704.
Support was seen by some brokers at around 720 while resistance was at 760 on Tuesday, brokers said.
